extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants (particularly in ASEAN Member States); patent office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on sufficiency of disclosure (enablement, best mode, support, clarity) and detailed procedures and criteria for conducting patent prior-art searches. Covers examiner judgment, search scope, databases, languages, analogous fields, and handling of claim types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing, the application must supply a sufficient disclosure in respect of the invention as claimed with regard to all of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims define the invention in terms of parameters, the application must include a clear description of the methods used to determine those parameter values unless a PSIA would know which method to use or all methods yield the same result. An examiner finding insufficiency cannot be cured after the fact by adding further examples that introduce added subject-matter; remedy may include restricting claims to embodiments sufficiently described and deleting descriptions of other embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency requires substantiated serious doubts
rubrics_metrics.description: An objection of lack of sufficient disclosure presupposes serious doubts which are substantiated by verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invention must be described in terms of structure and also function unless functions are immediately apparent. Consider whether undue experimentation is required (see listed factors). More details referenced in PCT ISPE GL 5.48–5.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for undue experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to be considered in determining whether undue experimentation is needed to carry out the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider (i) breadth of the claims; (ii) nature of the invention; (iii) general knowledge of a PSIA; (iv) level of predictability in the art; (v) amount of direction provided in the application, including references to prior art; and (vi) amount of experimentation required to carry out the claimed invention on the basis of the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreparable fundamental insufficiency (cannot be carried out)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally applications suffer a fundamental insufficiency such that the invention cannot be carried out by a PSIA and this is essentially irreparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two specific instances: (a) where successful performance depends on chance (results not reproducible or totally unreliable); distinguish from processes with some failure rate provided satisfactory parts can be sorted e.g., by nondestructive testing; (b) where successful performance is inherently impossible because contrary to well-established physical laws (e.g., perpetual motion machine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on sufficiency issues
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, the burden of proof for sufficiency of disclosure lies with the party raising the objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are serious doubts about performing or repeating the invention, the burden of proof, or at least a demonstration that success is credible, rests with the applicant or patent proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS require the specification to set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best mode requirement is subjective: the inventor must disclose the best way known to them at filing (not necessarily the absolute best). The best mode imposes an affirmative obligation and is separate and distinct from the enablement requirement (enablement concerns teaching a PSIA to implement; best mode concerns quality/honesty of disclosure). TRIPS Art.29 allows members to require indication of best mode but makes enablement compulsory while best mode is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and support of claims linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the disclosure is insufficient to enable a PSIA to carry out the claimed invention, the claims may be too broad to be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficiency may therefore lead to objections both under sufficiency (enablement) and under support of claims; examiner should consider both requirements together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure vs clarity distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a balance between lack of clarity and lack of disclosure to be assessed on the merits of each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguity in claims will lead to lack of disclosure objection if the whole scope of the claim is affected making it impossible to carry out the invention; otherwise a lack of clarity objection is more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trade names and proper names in disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of trade mark, company name, trade name or similar words to refer to materials is undesirable if they merely denote origin or a range of products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such words are used, the product must be sufficiently identified without reliance on the trade name to enable a PSIA to carry out the invention at filing. Exception: where such words have become internationally accepted as standard descriptive terms with precise meaning (examples provided) they may be allowed without further identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of patent search
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of search is to discover relevant prior art(s). Searching authority must attempt to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant prior art = everything capable of assisting in determining novelty and inventive step. Prior art = everything made available to the public anywhere by disclosure prior to the relevant date. Examiner encouraged to cite prior art that may assist in assessing sufficiency, support and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search completeness and examiner resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Search and preparation of search opinion depend on the search for the state of the art on which patentability assessment is based; search must be as complete and effective as possible within necessary limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations include unity of invention and other considerations. Search normally by one examiner but multiple examiners may be necessary for inventions requiring searching widely dispersed specialized fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion at time of search (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice is for examiner to provide a written opinion on novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability at the same time as producing the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information helps the applicant know how to amend the application and overcome objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the search (no amendments before search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the search has started or after request for search/examination submitted, there is no right to amend the application until after the search has been established; search carried out on basis of search copy submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only obvious mistakes may be corrected. Examiner should search based on filed content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search options and public database accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Search options, preferably online, are critical for assessing patentability and clearance searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All AMS except Myanmar provide online search options; public search databases in some AMS offer English interface (best practice). ASEAN Patentscope and WIPO Patentscope are one-stop shops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of earlier search/examination reports (priority cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: For priority-based applicants, applicant may submit earlier search/examination report and/or written opinion and/or granted patent to the receiving patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving office may invite applicant to furnish S&E report within reasonable time. If earlier search carried out by another office, the authority may take results into account (may replace part of the search). Examiner should consider fields of search and cited documents to determine relevance and assist selection of databases/classifications/terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages used in conducting searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Both English and the country's official language should at least be used by AMS patent offices in conducting searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional languages (e.g., JP, DE) should be used whenever possible to make search more complete and effective. Machine-translated collections (Espacenet) can assist English searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Databases and resources to be used
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching authority may use a mixture of non-commercial and commercial databases and internet resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet disclosures are prior art; use of Internet and non-patent literature may be necessary. Search Guidance IPDL (WIPO) lists resources. Examiner should consult all documents in the field irrespective of language/age/type but may omit segments with very low likelihood of relevance for reasons of economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and family member selection judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: For reasons of economy, the examiner should exercise judgment to omit segments of search files/databases unlikely to yield relevant documents; consult only one patent family member unless good reason to consult another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mechanically search everything; limit by technological development period or family member relevance, unless substantial differences expected or earlier publication date demands citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of search to other resources where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Search may have to be extended to other listed resources or analogous fields based on outcome of initial search fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The need to extend must be judged in each case, taking into account initial search outcome and probability of finding relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of IPC places and classification strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification places included in the search should be selected in all directly relevant fields and, if necessary, in analogous fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using IPC, include higher subdivisions allowing abstraction where technically justified and parallel subdivisions, bearing in mind increasing unrelatedness; select classifications most appropriate to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy and prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Various relevant search strategies may be possible; examiner should exercise judgment based on experience and knowledge of resources to select appropriate strategies and order of consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to main technical field of application and to resources/strategies with highest probability of finding relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet search use and confidentiality caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Search can cover Internet sources (online journals, databases, websites); extent depends on case and systematic internet search may be regularly necessary in some technical fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In information/software fields internet searches often necessary. When searching unpublished applications, take care not to disclose confidential information via search terms — choose keywords that avoid disclosing invention rather than long claim text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of analogous fields in search
rubrics_metrics.description: Field of search should, where appropriate, include analogous fields consistent with the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine analogous fields by necessary function or use of claimed invention, not only specific functions indicated. Consider: (i) fields where same/similar structure expected for different use; (ii) fields to which a generic concept pertains; (iii) art within inventor's activity relevant to problem; (iv) fields relevant to function/utility inherent in claimed subject-matter. Extension decision rests on whether a reasonable lack-of-inventive-step objection could be established from likely finds in those fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search parameters and coverage (what to search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search parameters may cover IPC, keywords and drawings; search coverage may include abstracts, claims, title, description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When beginning the search, analyze claims in light of description and drawings to determine subject of the claimed invention; search directed to invention as interpreted with regard to description and with emphasis on inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of claims for search direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner first critically analyzes the claims in the light of description and drawings to determine subject of claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search is directed to the invention defined by the claims as interpreted with due regard to the description/drawings and inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full coverage principle (subject-matter scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle and insofar as possible and reasonable the search should cover the entire subject-matter to which the claims are directed or might reasonably be expected to be directed after amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy considerations may justify certain restrictions (e.g., broad claim with many examples where it is not possible to foresee which will be subject of amended claims). Example: if description gives detailed transistor circuit but claims functionally, the search must include that detailed circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling speculative or unduly wide claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort beyond what is supported by the description is needed for unduly wide or speculative claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not extend to unrelated technologies merely due to broad wording, except where it is probable that extended search could produce a document that establishes lack of novelty or inventive step. If meaningful search of unsupported claim subject-matter can be done without much extra effort and scope is not unduly wide, extend the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dependent claims in search
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for independent claim(s) must take into account subject-matter of all dependent claims; dependent claims are interpreted as restricted by features of claims they depend on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If independent claim is novel from search, dependent claims are considered novel for search purposes. If novelty/inventive step of main claim questioned, may need to expand search to assess novelty of dependent claim features. No special search for well-known features unless easily found documentary evidence should be cited. Dependent claims adding further features constitute combination claims and should be addressed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of particular claim types and the role of preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Words of a claim read as a PSIA would understand; in two-part claims preamble is a limitation on scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some circumstances extend search to technological background including (i) preamble portion before 'characterised by' or 'the improvement comprising'; (ii) state of prior art as explained in introduction of description; (iii) general technological background ('general state of the art'). Consider particular forms such as product-by-process and two-part claims accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination claims and sub-combinations search
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims characterised by combinations of elements (A, B and C), the search should be directed to the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching classification units, also search sub-combinations (AB, AC, BC) and individual elements (A, B, C) in those units at the same time. Additional classification units for sub-combinations or individual elements should be searched only if necessary to establish novelty of an element to assess inventive step of the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different categories of claims in search
rubrics_metrics.description: When application contains claims of different categories that comply with unity, all must be included in the search; where only one category present it may be desirable to include others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a reference describing a process but only claiming the product might be classified under product subclass; therefore, when searching for a process it may be necessary to search for the product as well. In chemical claims, starting products may form part of the state of the art and need not be searched; intermediate products only when claimed; final products are highly recommended to be searched unless evidently known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy preliminary steps and handling cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the application should be examined if they are cited as starting point, state of the art, alternative solutions or necessary for correct understanding; disregard citations that relate only to details not directly relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a cited document is unpublished/inaccessible and essential for meaningful search, the searching authority may request the applicant to provide a copy within time limits. If no copy received, attempt search and indicate if meaningful search could not be carried out as a whole or needed restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and title consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should consider the abstract (with title and figure for publication) and determine its definitive contents no later than completion of the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should relate to the application as filed; examiner should finalize abstract content by search report completion to ensure accurate public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification according to IPC
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the abstract, the examiner should classify the application according to at least the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification assists field-of-search selection and should be performed early in search process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a written search statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may prepare a written search statement defining subject of their search as precisely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may serve but may need generalisation to cover all aspects and embodiments. Consider exclusions from search and lack of unity; if unity not satisfied, examiner may choose to conduct search on first invention or inventive concept only. Examiner should avoid restricting search unless unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The closest prior art is the single reference disclosing the combination of features that constitutes the most promising starting point for development leading to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closest prior art should be directed to similar purpose/effect or belong to same/closely related field, be capable of carrying out claimed function, and be selected based on examiner's interpretation of claims. Examiner should also cite prior art likely to assist in determining sufficiency and support throughout the claimed field.
